vo_01a.text: I'm Chris. Some afternoons I want to go outside, but I don't know where to go.

vo_01b.text: And my friends? Mostly homebodies. 'We should hang out' never turns into a plan.

vo_02.text: So I built StrollCall. Tell it how long you have and what you feel like, and it plans a short walk worth taking: on your own, or with a friend.

vo_03.text: I just say what I want. Muse Voice transcribes it, and Muse Glimmer, an open-weights model I host on Modal, turns it into a plan the route engine understands, in about half a second.

vo_04.text: While I walk, the map fills the screen, and my walking buddy listens. When I ask for a coffee stop, Muse Spark picks a tool, the planner re-routes, and only real, open places come back.

vo_05.text: Walking is better with someone. I send one link. My friend doesn't need an app: one tap, and they can say what they'd like too.

vo_06.text: Muse Spark balances both of our wishes and explains the trade-off. And the meeting point is fair by walking time, not by distance on a map: here, the map's midpoint leaves us 4.8 minutes apart; ours gets us there within a minute.

vo_07.text: Under the hood: a walking graph of New York with 139,106 points, built from OpenStreetMap, plans in milliseconds. Meta models handle the human side: Muse Glimmer reads wishes, Muse Spark negotiates and ranks, Muse Image draws the invite, Muse Voice listens.

vo_08.text: Every evaluation was committed before it ran. 12 of 12 test pairs got the right outcome. Meta's reading caught 10 of 10 wishes, against 7 for keyword rules. And a checker throws out any claim our data can't back up.
